content: Venous hum, also known as Nun's murmur or Bruit de diable, is a benign phenomenon caused by blood flow over the jugular veins. At rest, approximately 20% of the cardiac output passes through the internal carotid and vertebral arteries. This phenomenon can produce a continuous humming noise. The sound is typically heard in the upper chest region, near the clavicle. It can be distinguished from cardiac murmurs by placing a finger on the jugular vein, which either abolishes or alters the murmur. In contrast, cardiac-origin murmurs remain unaffected by this maneuver. Additionally, the intensity of the murmur is position-dependent. It may change if the patient lies in a supine position or turns their head to one side.
